Partial aniridia, cerebellar ataxia and intellectual disability define Gillespie syndrome; isolated additional anomalies lack population frequency evidence.

Echinococcus larvae form organ-occupying cysts; liver involvement occurs in ~60-75%. Pulmonary involvement is generally below 30%; other sites are uncommon.

Glycosylation defect impairs leukocyte adhesion; severe intellectual disability is defining and cerebral atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Recurrent infections are separate diseases.

Immune-mediated target skin lesions define EM; erosive oral mucositis occurs in roughly 25-60%, near the threshold. Ocular damage is uncommon.
PLCB1-related epileptic encephalopathy causes seizures and developmental regression; muscle stiffening reflects neurologic dysfunction.

Zona pellucida defects affect oocytes and fertility; sex hormone levels are normal.
Obstruction affects the renal arteries; hypertension is cardiovascular. Renal parenchymal damage is not established as a common defining feature.
Impaired neuromuscular junction transmission defines this umbrella; autoimmune mechanisms do not apply to every major subgroup.
Tongue hypoplasia and limb reduction define the syndrome; structural fingernail abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Intellectual disability occurs in only 5-29%.
Endometrial granulomatous inflammation has infectious or immune-mediated causes, including tuberculosis and sarcoidosis; the reproductive site has no organ axis.
